def-proper-scoring-rule:
## Definition

For an integer $K\ge2$, let the label set be $\mathcal Y=\{1,\ldots,K\}$ and let $\Delta_K=\{q\in[0,1]^K:\sum_{j=1}^Kq_j=1\}$. A finite-label score loss is a function $S:\Delta_K\times\mathcal Y\to[0,+\infty]$ whose section $q\mapsto S(q,j)$ is Borel measurable for every label $j$. If the true label distribution is $p\in\Delta_K$ and the reported forecast is $q\in\Delta_K$, its expected score loss is $\bar S(p,q)=\sum_{j=1}^Kp_jS(q,j)$, where a term with $p_j=0$ contributes zero even when $S(q,j)=+\infty$. The loss is **proper** if $\bar S(p,p)\le\bar S(p,q)$ for every $p,q\in\Delta_K$, and **strictly proper** if equality implies $q=p$. The logarithmic loss is $S_{\log}(q,j)=-\log q_j$, with $-\log0=+\infty$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm; the Brier loss is $S_{\mathrm B}(q,j)=\sum_{i=1}^K(q_i-\mathbf1_{\{i=j\}})^2$.
lem-jensen-for-simplex-pairs:
## Statement

For an integer $K\ge2$, let $\Delta_K=\{p\in[0,1]^K:\sum_{j=1}^Kp_j=1\}$ and $C=\Delta_K\times\Delta_K\subset\mathbb R^{2K}$. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space, let $Z=(U,V):\Omega\to C$ be measurable, and let $\psi:C\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and jointly convex, meaning $\psi(\lambda z+(1-\lambda)w)\le\lambda\psi(z)+(1-\lambda)\psi(w)$ for all $z,w\in C$ and $\lambda\in[0,1]$. Define $\mathbb E Z$ coordinatewise. Then $\mathbb E Z=(\mathbb E U,\mathbb E V)\in C$ and
$$\psi(\mathbb E U,\mathbb E V)\le\mathbb E[\psi(U,V)].$$
lem-negative-root-power-is-convex:
## Statement

For every real $s\ge1$, the function $\varphi_s:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ defined by $\varphi_s(t)=-t^{1/s}$, with $0^{1/s}=0$, is convex.
def-probability-calibration:
## Definition

Let $K\ge2$, let $Y$ be a random variable into the finite label set $\{1,\ldots,K\}$ with its full power-set sigma-algebra on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$, and let $G=(G_1,\ldots,G_K):\Omega\to\Delta_K$ be a measurable forecast, where $\Delta_K=\{p\in[0,1]^K:\sum_jp_j=1\}$. The forecast is **fully reliable** if for every label $j$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\Delta_K$,
$$\mathbb P(Y=j,\ G\in B)=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{G\in B\}}G_j].$$
It is **classwise calibrated** if for every $j$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq[0,1]$,
$$\mathbb P(Y=j,\ G_j\in B)=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{G_j\in B\}}G_j].$$
For the **top-confidence calibration** condition, define $C=\max_jG_j$ and $\widehat Y=\min\{j:G_j=C\}$, so ties go to the smallest label. The forecast is top-confidence calibrated if for every Borel set $B\subseteq[0,1]$,
$$\mathbb P(Y=\widehat Y,\ C\in B)=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{C\in B\}}C].$$
A measurable function $r:\Delta_K\to\Delta_K$ is a **calibration function** for $G$ if for every $j$ and every Borel set $B\subseteq\Delta_K$,
$$\mathbb P(Y=j,\ G\in B)=\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{G\in B\}}r_j(G)].$$
When such a function is supplied and $d:\Delta_K\times\Delta_K\to[0,+\infty)$ is measurable, the **expected calibration error with discrepancy $d$** is $\eta_d=\mathbb E[d(r(G),G)]$.
lem-finite-label-conditional-probability:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let a supervised prediction problem have a measurable instance space $(\mathsf X,\Sigma_X)$, finite label set $\mathcal Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_K\}$ with distinct labels, the full power-set sigma-algebra on $\mathcal Y$, and $K\ge2$, and joint probability law $P$ on $\mathsf X\times\mathcal Y$; let $X$ and $Y$ be its coordinate random variables and let $\mathcal G=\{X^{-1}(A):A\in\Sigma_X\}$, the sigma-algebra generated by $X$. There is a measurable function $\eta=(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_K):\mathsf X\to\Delta_K$, where $\Delta_K=\{p\in[0,1]^K:\sum_jp_j=1\}$, such that for every label index $j$ and $A\in\Sigma_X$,
$$P(X\in A,\ Y=y_j)=\mathbb E[\eta_j(X)\mathbf1_{\{X\in A\}}].$$
thm-log-and-brier-strict-propriety:
## Statement

For every $K\ge2$ and $p,q\in\Delta_K$, the logarithmic and Brier losses in the definition of finite-label score loss satisfy $\bar S(p,p)\le\bar S(p,q)$, with equality only when $q=p$. The expected logarithmic loss at the truthful forecast is finite, including when some coordinates of $p$ vanish.
cor-any-feature-induces-calibrated-forec:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let a finite-label supervised prediction problem have measurable instance space $(\mathsf X,\Sigma_X)$ and finite labels $\mathcal Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_K\}$ with the full power-set sigma-algebra, where $K\ge2$. Identify label $y_j$ with its index $j$ when applying numbered-label calibration, so forecast coordinate $j$ always represents the event $Y=y_j$. For every measurable feature $T:\mathsf X\to(\mathsf Z,\Sigma_Z)$, there is a measurable $\eta_T:\mathsf Z\to\Delta_K$ such that $G=\eta_T(T(X))$ is a conditional class-probability forecast given $T(X)$ and is fully reliable. This includes the identity feature and a constant feature.
thm-posterior-forecast-minimizes-scoring:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $X$ and a finite label $Y\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$ with the full power-set sigma-algebra, $K\ge2$, have a joint probability law on standard-Borel spaces. For a proper finite-label score loss $S$, a measurable posterior forecast $G(x)=P(Y\in\cdot\mid X=x)$ minimizes the expected score loss among all measurable forecasts. If $S$ is strictly proper and the posterior forecast has finite expected score loss, equality of risk for another forecast $q(X)$ implies $q(X)=G(X)$ almost surely.
def-classification-calibration-of-a-surr:
## Definition

Let $Y\in\{-1,+1\}$ be the label in a supervised prediction problem with the full power-set sigma-algebra on this binary label set, and choose the finite-label conditional probability function ordered as $(-1,+1)$; write $\eta(x)=\eta_{+1}(x)$. Let $\Phi:\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$ be finite, convex and nondecreasing. It is continuous on $\mathbb R$; extend it to $\overline{\mathbb R}=\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ by its one-sided monotone limits, which may equal $+\infty$. The resulting extended function is Borel measurable. For $u\in\overline{\mathbb R}$ define the conditional margin risk
$$L_\Phi(x,u)=\eta(x)\Phi(-u)+(1-\eta(x))\Phi(u),$$
using $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$ at endpoints. A measurable extended-real conditional minimizer is a measurable $h_\Phi^*:\mathsf X\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ satisfying $L_\Phi(x,h_\Phi^*(x))\le L_\Phi(x,u)$ for every $x$ and every $u\in\overline{\mathbb R}$. For a measurable real-valued score $h$, its margin loss is $\ell_\Phi(h(x),y)=\Phi(-yh(x))$, its surrogate risk is $L_\Phi(h)=\mathbb E[\Phi(-Yh(X))]$, and its conditional-minimum risk is $L_\Phi^*=\mathbb E[L_\Phi(X,h_\Phi^*(X))]$. Under the zero-score-is-error convention, its classification risk is $R_{01}(h)=P(Yh(X)\le0)$, and the Bayes classification risk is $R_{01}^*=\mathbb E[\min\{\eta(X),1-\eta(X)\}]$. Write $h^*(x)=\eta(x)-\tfrac12$ for the centered conditional class probability.
thm-binned-calibration-estimator-limits:
## Statement

Let $Y$ be a random variable into $\{1,\ldots,K\}$ with its full power-set sigma-algebra, $K\ge2$, and let $G\in\Delta_K$ be a random forecast with measurable calibration function $r:\Delta_K\to\Delta_K$. Let $d:\Delta_K\times\Delta_K\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and satisfy $d(p,p)=0$. For a finite data-independent Borel partition $\mathcal P$ of $\Delta_K$, draw an iid sequence $(G_i,Y_i)$ from the joint law of $(G,Y)$, let $V_i=e_{Y_i}$ be the corresponding standard basis vector, and form the empirical estimator
$$\widehat E_{n,\mathcal P}=\sum_{B\in\mathcal P}\frac{N_B}{n}\,d(\bar V_B,\bar G_B),$$
where $N_B=\#\{i\le n:G_i\in B\}$ and, when $N_B>0$, $\bar V_B$ and $\bar G_B$ are the sample averages in bin $B$; when $N_B=0$, set both to any fixed $q_0\in\Delta_K$. Define
$$E_{\mathcal P}=\sum_{B\in\mathcal P:P(G\in B)>0}P(G\in B)\,d\!\left(\mathbb E[r(G)\mid G\in B],\mathbb E[G\mid G\in B]\right).$$
For each fixed $\mathcal P$, $\widehat E_{n,\mathcal P}\to E_{\mathcal P}$ almost surely. If $d$ is additionally jointly convex, then $E_{\mathcal P}\le\mathbb E[d(r(G),G)]$. Without requiring convexity, if $\mathcal P_m$ is a sequence of finite data-independent Borel partitions with mesh tending to zero and $r$ is Lipschitz, then $E_{\mathcal P_m}\to\mathbb E[d(r(G),G)]$. Thus the iterated limit $\lim_{m\to\infty}\lim_{n\to\infty}\widehat E_{n,\mathcal P_m}$ equals the expected calibration error almost surely; no diagonal rate is asserted.
lem-binary-zero-one-risk-excess-with-zer:
## Statement

For a binary supervised problem with the full power-set sigma-algebra on $Y\in\{-1,+1\}$, conditional positive-label probability $\eta$, and any measurable real-valued score $h$, use $R_{01}(h)=P(Yh(X)\le0)$ and $R_{01}^*=\mathbb E\min\{\eta(X),1-\eta(X)\}$. Then
$$R_{01}(h)-R_{01}^*=2\mathbb E\!\left[\left|\eta(X)-\tfrac12\right|\mathbf1_{\{h(X)(\eta(X)-\tfrac12)\le0\}}\right]+\mathbb E\!\left[\min\{\eta(X),1-\eta(X)\}\mathbf1_{\{h(X)=0\}}\right].$$
fs-unadjusted-surrogate-regret-bound:
## Statement

The following proposed implication is false. In the binary-surrogate setup, take $R_{01}(h)=P(Yh(X)\le0)$, so zero scores count as errors. If $s\ge1,c>0$ and for every $x$,
$$|\eta(x)-1/2|^s\le c[L_\Phi(x,0)-L_\Phi(x,h_\Phi^*(x))],$$
then every measurable real-valued score $h$ with finite surrogate risk satisfies
$$R_{01}(h)-R_{01}^*\le2c[L_\Phi(h)-L_\Phi^*]^{1/s}.$$
Even replacing $2c$ by $2c^{1/s}$ does not make this zero-remainder implication true under the stated zero-score-is-error convention.
thm-surrogate-regret-controls-classifica:
## Statement

Assume AC and the binary-surrogate setup, including a measurable extended-real conditional minimizer $h_\Phi^*$. Let $s\ge1$ and $c>0$. Suppose for every $x$,
$$\left|\eta(x)-\tfrac12\right|^s\le c\,[L_\Phi(x,0)-L_\Phi(x,h_\Phi^*(x))].$$
Then every measurable real-valued score $h$ with finite surrogate risk satisfies the sound zero-score-is-error bound
$$R_{01}(h)-R_{01}^*\le 2c^{1/s}[L_\Phi(h)-L_\Phi^*]^{1/s}+\mathbb E\!\left[\min\{\eta(X),1-\eta(X)\}\mathbf1_{\{h(X)=0\}}\right].$$

In particular, if $P(h(X)=0)=0$, the correction vanishes. Define instead the label classifier $f_h(x)=+1$ for $h(x)\ge0$ and $f_h(x)=-1$ for $h(x)<0$, and write $R_+(h)=P(f_h(X)\ne Y)$. For all scores covered above, including scores with zeros,
$$R_+(h)-R_{01}^*\le 2c^{1/s}[L_\Phi(h)-L_\Phi^*]^{1/s}.$$
Equivalently, parameterizing the same margin premise by $|\eta(x)-1/2|^s\le a^s[L_\Phi(x,0)-L_\Phi(x,h_\Phi^*(x))]$ gives coefficient $2a$ in both inequalities, with the same zero-score correction when using $R_{01}$.
